newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks surge to record close on U.S. election.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks surge to record close on U.S. election.

text.p: Election fever swept Hong Kong stocks to record high levels on Wednesday, as investors viewed the results of Tuesday's U.S. election as a promise of stable economic policy and looked forward to a rally in U.S. stocks.

The Hang Seng index of blue chip stocks jumped to a new intra-day high of 12,779.11 before ending 272.77 points up at a record close of 12,775.47. Turnover surged to HK$10.29 billion compared to Tuesday's HK$7.48 billion.
"What is happening? One word - election," said Miles Remington, sales trader at Crosby Securities. "The result is filtering into the market as being the best of all worlds."

Democrat Bill Clinton won re-election as U.S. president on Tuesday while the Republican party apparently maintained control of Congress. Analysts said U.S. stocks and bonds were likely to rally on the news.
"People are viewing this as being positive because it will keep both sides in check," said Remington. "The belief here is that there will be a very strong move in the bond market."

Wednesday's Hang Seng intra-day record beat Tuesday's peak of 12,616.37 points. Turnover was the highest since September 24 when placements by Henderson Land and COSCO Pacific boosted market turnover to HK$10.38 billion.

"It looks like the market has the momentum to go higher. I don't think we should have any difficulty going to 13,000 (points) in the near term," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.
"The most significant thing which has been developing is the downward trend of the (U.S.) long bond yield and this is extremely positive," he said.
The U.S. long bond yield closed at its lowest level in 7-1/2 months on Tuesday at 6.59 percent.
However, analysts said there could be some profit-taking in the local market on Thursday.
"The problem now is people will be looking for value. Fear of a major correction could raise its ugly head if we continue to see the market move at this pace," said Remington.
Wednesday's 272.77 point gain was the biggest point gain in the Hang Seng since March 19 when the index rose 279.22 points.
Shares in HSBC Holdings jumped HK$4.50 to HK$163.00 and Hang Seng Bank advanced HK$3.50 to HK$94.00.
Sun Hung Kai Properties was also a strong mover, up HK$2.14 at HK$87.75. Great Eagle Holdings rose HK$1.55 to HK$28.35 and Swire Pacific added HK$2.00 to HK$68.75.
